content: The hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 plays a critical role in the metabolism of various drugs. Below are detailed interactions between specific drugs and the enzyme CYP3A4, as well as recommendations for monitoring and therapy adjustments: 1. Cobicistat and Doxepin Cream: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of doxepin cream by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Darunavir and Doxorubicin: Darunavir elevates the levels or effects of doxorubicin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Cobicistat and Dronabinol: Cobicistat raises the levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. Use caution and monitor. 4. Darunavir and Doxorubicin Liposomal: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of liposomal doxorubicin via CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Darunavir and Dronabinol: Darunavir enhances the levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Dronedarone and Darunavir: Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 7. Darunavir and Drospirenone: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of drospirenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended. 8. Darunavir and Duvelisib: Darunavir raises the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 9. Duvelisib and Darunavir: Duvelisib increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 10. Cobicistat and Efavirenz: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both darunavir and efavirenz increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 11. Darunavir and Elagolix: Darunavir elevates the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg twice daily with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 12. Cobicistat and Elagolix: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg twice daily with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 13. Elagolix and Darunavir: Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered. 14. Elagolix and Cobicistat: The combination of elagolix (a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer) with cobicistat (a CYP3A4 inhibitor and substrate) may increase elagolix levels and decrease cobicistat levels. Refer to prescribing information for dosage adjustments. 15. Darunavir and Eletriptan: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of eletriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 16. Cobicistat and Elvitegravir/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of this combination therapy by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 17. Darunavir and Elvitegravir/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of this combination therapy by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 18. Cobicistat and Encorafenib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Darunavir and Encorafenib: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Cobicistat and Enfortumab Vedotin: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Darunavir and Enfortumab Vedotin: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 22. Darunavir and Enzalutamide: Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 23. Cobicistat and Erlotinib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of erlotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the erlotinib dose by 50 mg increments if co-administration cannot be avoided. 24. Darunavir and Erlotinib: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of erlotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Erythromycin and Darunavir: Erythromycin increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 26. Cobicistat and Escitalopram: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of escitalopram by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 27. Darunavir and Estradiol: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Cobicistat and Estradiol Vaginal: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Darunavir and Ethinyl Estradiol: Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended. 30. Darunavir and Fentanyl: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fentanyl by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 31. Cobicistat and Fentanyl: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fentanyl by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 32. Darunavir and Fluticasone: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fluticasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 33. Cobicistat and Fluticasone: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluticasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 34. Darunavir and Fluoxetine: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fluoxetine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 35. Cobicistat and Fluoxetine: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluoxetine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 36. Darunavir and Flurazepam: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of flurazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 37. Cobicistat and Flurazepam: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of flurazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 38. Darunavir and Grapefruit: Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 39. Darunavir and Insulin: Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 40. Darunavir and Isoniazid: Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 41. Darunavir and Imipramine: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 42. Cobicistat and Imipramine: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 43. Darunavir and Indinavir: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Darunavir and Hydrocodone: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 45. Cobicistat and Hydrocodone: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 46. Darunavir and Ifosfamide: Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 47. Cobicistat and Ifosfamide: Cobicistat decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. This list highlights the importance of monitoring drug interactions involving CYP3A4 metabolism, as they can significantly impact drug efficacy and safety.
